Followups

Backlog spillover discovered during implementation. Keep items PR-sized when possible.

Critical convention. Every followup must carry a data-priority attribute. Three buckets:
  • blocks-release: cannot ship v1 without this.
  • nice-to-have: improves the product but does not block.
  • polish: post-release cleanup.

How to add a followup

<section data-f="F-NNN" data-priority="blocks-release|nice-to-have|polish">
  <h3>F-NNN: Short title</h3>
  <dl>
    <dt>Context</dt><dd>one or two sentences on why this came up.</dd>
    <dt>Blocker (if any)</dt><dd>the condition that prevents working on this now.</dd>
    <dt>Unblock condition</dt><dd>what has to be true to start.</dd>
    <dt>PR / Dot reference</dt><dd>#N or dots-N (when picked up)</dd>
  </dl>
</section>

Keep F-NNN IDs monotonically increasing. When a followup ships, leave the entry in place and append a <dt>Resolved</dt><dd>PR #N</dd> entry. Never delete.

F-223: Skip the browser matrix for documentation-only diffs

Context
Noticed on 2026-08-03 while landing #311, a three-file change under .dots/ with no source, config, or dependency edits. .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on a bare pull_request: with no paths or paths-ignore filter, and no job carries a changed-files condition, so all 17 jobs (25 checks after matrix expansion) ran anyway: a full Next.js production build, two Critical E2E shards, ten Functional Shadows, two Runtime Shadows plus the comparison, a Vercel preview deploy for Preview Smoke, and CodeQL. Three pushes on that PR meant roughly three passes over the matrix to validate HTML that no application code imports.
Blocker (if any)
None technical, but the obvious fix is a trap. A workflow-level paths-ignore makes skipped jobs report as never-run rather than passed, so any of them that are required status checks leave the PR permanently unsatisfiable. This repo already merges with --admin because the AutoReview ruleset carries an unsatisfiable code_scanning rule, so a change that makes branch protection harder to satisfy would compound an existing problem rather than sit beside it.
Unblock condition
Ready: add a changed-files detection job, then gate the browser matrix, build, and preview smoke on it with job-level if: conditions, keeping every required check reporting a green no-op on the skipped path so branch protection stays satisfiable. Decide explicitly which paths count as documentation-only; .dots/ and docs/ are the obvious members, and any path that feeds the build or the test harness is not. Acceptance: a docs-only PR reports every required check green without running the browser matrix, a PR touching src/ still runs the full gate, and a PR touching both runs the full gate. Prove the first two with real PRs rather than by reading the workflow.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-08-03 during #311. Dot VibeBots-f-223-skip-ec944b00.
Placement decision 2026-08-04
This entry carries data-priority="polish" but was committed under blocks-release, which made pnpm check:followups fail on main from the moment #311 merged. The entry stays exactly where it is, because primaries are never relocated. F-222: The death playback should own its own lifetime

Context
Found while root causing a player report on 2026-08-02: a fatal fall played a few rows, then the bot was pulled back up and respawned at the surface. useMineDeathPlaybackBridge in src/components/mine-death-playback.ts subscribes to the store and drops the live playback on any tick change whose result is not a collapse. That is the whole tear-down rule, and tick is not a player-action counter: shop purchases, rail resyncs, cloud adoptions, and the trip bank all bump or reset it. The bank was the trigger that fired on every single death, and this slice removed it by deferring the bank until the trip report is dismissed. The bridge itself is unchanged, so a tick-changing store write whose result is not a collapse still tears the playback down if it lands inside the playback window. The second half is resetJump in mine-canvas.tsx: it reads lastResult.collapsed to decide the end-of-playback snap, so a write that clears lastResult also turns that snap into a glide up through solid rock.
Blocker (if any)
None technical. It needs a signal the bridge can trust, since tick conflates player actions with store housekeeping. Either a separate action counter that only move advances, or the playback holding its own timers and ignoring store churn entirely until its impact or timeout path ends it.
Unblock condition
Pick the signal, land it, and pin it with a test that resets the store mid-playback and asserts the playback survives and still ends with a snap rather than a glide. Rule 10 applies: assert the rendered data-minerY keeps descending across the reset rather than only that a flag is still set.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-08-02 while fixing the fatal-fall yank in #310. No Dot exists for this slice.

F-220: Stop a read advancing the replay counter, and confirm banking in production

Context
The 2026-07-29 save-loss fix made an ore-less carving trip bank, which is the real cause of the reported loss, and made a trip-index divergence prompt instead of silently discarding the device's work. Two things it deliberately did not touch. First, GET /api/mine/world runs trip_count = trip_count + 1 inside its elevator-rail install and repair path (src/app/api/mine/world/route.ts), and POST /api/elevator/upgrade bumps it too. That counter is the bank route's replay-protection compare-and-set, so a read (and an unrelated surface purchase) can invalidate a player's in-flight trip. It is a deliberate invalidation signal, not an accident: the server changed the world under the client, so client trips replaying the old diff are genuinely stale. But one counter is carrying two meanings, trips banked and world revision. Second, production logs across 72 hours contained zero POST /api/mine/bank requests, which is how the drift went unnoticed; there is no telemetry that would have made a silent absence of banking visible.
Blocker (if any)
None technical.
Unblock condition
Two pieces. First, decide whether to split the counter: a separate world revision that invalidates client trips, leaving trip_count to mean only trips banked, so a rail repair or an elevator buy no longer invalidates an in-flight trip and no GET mutates the value the bank guard compares. With banking now firing on every carving trip the drift window is much smaller, so this is a correctness and clarity fix rather than an active data-loss one. Second, confirm in production that banking now happens: watch for POST /api/mine/bank after an ore-less digging trip, and consider a monitoring counter for accepted and rejected banks so a future regression to zero is visible rather than silent. Worth also checking whether an ore-less bank on every surface arrival is a request rate anyone minds on mobile.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-07-29 by the save-loss fix. The load-path half of the fix is recorded in the same progress-log entry.
Telemetry half shipped, counter half decided (2026-07-29)
The observability gap turned out not to be the one this entry first described. The bank route already logs a cash_out_succeeded event plus about nineteen distinct failure codes, so accepted and rejected banks were always instrumented. What no server-side counter can see is a request that is never sent: a bank that is skipped or refused leaves nothing behind, and that silence is identical to nobody playing. Adding another per-request counter would have been silent in exactly the case that mattered. Shipped instead: a new surfaced_carving_unbanked client diagnostic. When a trip that changed the world reaches the surface and the cash-out settles as error or unavailable, the client reports it through the existing bounded /api/mine/diagnostics pipeline with the settled state and the size of the log stranded on the device, deduped per trip so an offline player reports once rather than on every surface arrival. That makes the absence visible from the only place that can observe it.
Counter split: recommended, not done, and one hazard for whoever does it
Decision on the question this entry posed: do NOT split the counter as part of the save-loss work, and treat it as a clarity fix rather than a data-loss one. Evidence. The bank route replays a submitted trip over the server's CURRENT stored diff, not the client's, so a world the server repaired underneath an in-flight trip does not actually corrupt a later bank; the trip_count bump is a resync signal rather than replay safety. The GET bump is gated on elevator_rail_installed_at IS NULL OR railNeedsRepair, so it fires roughly once per player rather than on every read. Banking now happens on every carving trip, which shrinks the in-flight window that can drift, and a divergence no longer destroys work: it raises the conflict prompt. So the remaining defect is one counter carrying two meanings, which is worth fixing for clarity but no longer costs anyone their progress. The hazard, which is the non-obvious part: loadLocalTrip rejects and DELETES any saved trip whose mineVersion does not match, so adding a required world-revision field to SavedTrip and bumping MINE_VERSION would wipe every player's in-flight trip on upgrade, which is precisely the harm this whole arc exists to stop. Any split must carry the new field as OPTIONAL, with an absent value on an older save reading as in step rather than as a divergence.
Player confirmation (2026-07-29, PR #306)
The reporter confirmed the fix on the same signed-in mobile installed app that showed the loss: an ore-less digging trip now survives killing and restarting the app. That closes the first half of the unblock condition, the part asking whether banking actually happens in production. What remains is the durable half: this was confirmed by a human replaying the exact scenario, not by any signal the project owns. A silent return to zero banks would still be invisible, which is how the original bug reached a player rather than CI, so the monitoring counter for accepted and rejected banks is still worth adding. The counter split (a read advancing the replay-protection value) is untouched and stays the other half of this entry.

F-219: Confirm the raid melee balance in a playtest and an executed raid e2e

Context
User direction 2026-07-27 turned live raids into a melee fight: Clanker bodies pursue the miner's live position continuously, contact is a bite against a 100-point health bar instead of an instant loss, and the pickaxe fights back. The stated tuning target is that a level-2 pickaxe should let a player fend off one Clanker but probably not two. The shipped constants hit that target on paper and a unit test pins the arithmetic (a level-2 pick needs 4 strikes over ~2s to drop a tier-1 Clanker, costing about a third of the bar to one attacker and more than the whole bar to two), but arithmetic is not feel, and nothing here has been played by a human.
Blocker (if any)
None technical.
Unblock condition
Two pieces. First, an executed E2E-MINE-BUNKER-FP-0019. It is tagged @render, so it runs in neither the required Critical gate nor the advisory Functional Shadow shards, and only executes in the scheduled or manually dispatched Full E2E matrix. That is why the F-218 slice never got an executed run out of it either, and it means a raid rendering regression can sit unseen between scheduled runs. Dispatch a Full E2E run, and decide whether 0019 should be retagged @functional or have its tight polls widened the way 0025's were, so a slow runner cannot make it read as a raid regression. The new 0025 is @functional, ran green in the shadow shards, and also passes locally against a production build (health falls below full while the raid keeps running, and pickaxe strikes connect). Second, a playtest against production confirming the feel: that a lone Clanker is a winnable duel rather than a formality, that a pair genuinely threatens, that the pursuit reads as being chased rather than as bodies drifting, and that the lunge, knockback, health bar, and hurt pulse make each exchange legible. Retune LIVE_PICKAXE_BASE_DAMAGE, LIVE_PICKAXE_DAMAGE_PER_LEVEL, LIVE_PLAYER_BITE_BASE, LIVE_PLAYER_STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS, and the chase speeds from that evidence; they are provisional in the same sense as the surrounding energy model. Also worth watching: whether a standard Clanker at 2.6 cells/s against the miner's 3.0 walk makes kiting too safe in a fully dug room.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-07-27 by the raid melee-combat slice. Supersession of kill-on-contact is recorded as Q-032; the F-218 staging invariants (nothing invisible bites, the breach hop never bites) are preserved and re-pinned by tests in this slice.

F-218: Stage the live raid opening so the wave is visible and survivable

Context
User playtest 2026-07-22: I never see the clankers when I'm in the bunker and the time ends immediately. A pure-sim repro (Node driver over createLiveRaid/stepLiveRaid: fresh 7x5 claim, only the 3x3x3 spawn pocket dug, player standing on the pocket floor at depth 0) ends the 180-second raid LOST at tick 20 of 1080, about 3.3 seconds in. The wave spawns 1 to 4 cells outside the footprint on the depth-0 approach ring, walks the open approach around the claim, enters the open pocket, and the first contact kills the miner. The Clankers are invisible for nearly the entire approach because they travel outside the dug interior, so the fight reads as the timer ended for no reason. The verdict banner and cooldown countdown (package 0.1.283) made the OUTCOME readable; the opening pacing still loses an undefended bunker in seconds with nothing to see or do.
Blocker (if any)
None technical. Kill-on-contact, the energy model, and the client-run raid are GDD contract; the exact numbers are explicitly provisional (meant to be tuned in playtests), and this playtest is the tuning evidence.
Unblock condition
Stage the opening so the player can see the threat and react before it can kill: spawn the wave at the far edge of the approach ring instead of 1 cell out, stagger Clanker activation so arrivals spread across the opening seconds, and make the approach observable from inside (audio cue, HUD proximity hint, or a visible entry moment). Keep kill-on-contact and the energy model. Recommended default: spawn at APPROACH_MARGIN distance and activate one Clanker per action window. Prove with a sim-level test that a stationary fresh-claim player survives past the first visible entry, and with the raid e2e that a visible Clanker precedes the first possible loss.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-07-22 by the raid-cooldown-clarity slice (package 0.1.283). Dot VibeBots-f-218-stage-35695d31.
Progress update (2026-07-22)
Shipped the staged, visible invasion (package 0.1.284, user direction: render the clankers in the base and have them navigate in 3d to attack the player). Sim: a 6-second onset before anything acts, one Clanker activating per 2.5 seconds (LIVE_RAID_ONSET_TICKS, LIVE_CLANKER_ACTIVATION_STAGGER_TICKS), and a breach hold (LIVE_CLANKER_BREACH_HOLD_TICKS) so the hop that burrows into the claim cannot kill: the Clanker surfaces at its entry cell, inert and dodgeable, before it hunts. Render: per-Clanker inside/justEntered view flags drive a scale-in emergence with a burrow burst at the wall; bodies and XP pickups draw only inside the footprint, because every room face is solid rock and anything outside was phantom draw work. The worst case is now proven in the sim suite: a player standing ON the entry cell survives the breach hop and dies only if still there after the hold, and the undefended fresh claim breaches strictly before it can lose (stationary loss moved from tick 20 to tick 60; first visible entry ~9s, contact ~10s, remaining wave arriving every 2.5s). Deviation from the recommended default: spawns stay 1 to 4 cells out rather than at the ring edge, because pre-breach travel is invisible either way, the onset supplies the same pacing, and ring-edge spawns would break the turret-perimeter interactions the turret suite pins. Remaining before close: an executed raid e2e run (blocked in the remote session by F-217) and playtest confirmation that the pacing feels right.
Reconciliation with PR #285 (2026-07-22)
PR #285 (F-104, package 0.1.283) independently shipped the presentation half on main while this branch was in flight: interpolated face-plane room visibility, a burrow dust puff at the crossing, damped travel yaw, climb pitch, and death-burst pinning, all in a new bunker-fp-clanker-motion module. On merge, this branch adopted #285's render layer wholesale and dropped its own provisional render path (the inside/justEntered view flags and scale-in emergence described above never shipped; only their tests were removed with them). What this branch contributes on top of #285: the sim staging (inertUntilTick onset, stagger, and breach hold, which makes #285's dust crossing dodgeable instead of a same-hop kill) and room-gating for XP pickups, which #285 left drawing out in the shell rock. The release-note claims were renumbered around #285's 0.1.283: cooldown clarity is 0.1.284 and the staged invasion is 0.1.285.

F-217: Restore dependency installs in remote agent sessions

Context
A remote Claude Code session (2026-07-22) could not run pnpm install --frozen-lockfile: the GitHub credentials those sessions inject are scoped to this repository only, so fetching the tag-pinned @randroids-dojo/vibekit github dependency from codeload.github.com returned 403 and the install aborted (no proxy-policy denial was recorded, so the refusal came from GitHub authorization, not egress). Without node_modules nothing that needs the toolchain can run there: no typecheck, no Biome, no unit tests, no build, no Playwright, and no dependency bumps. The Dependency Upgrade Gate had just detected Next.js 16.2.11 over the pinned 16.2.10, and that bump had to be deferred for exactly this reason. VibeKit's Detect-new command is also unrunnable in such sessions: gh is absent and the VibeKit repository sits outside the session's GitHub scope.
Blocker (if any)
Access policy, not code: only the environment owner can widen a session's GitHub scope or provision VibeKit another way.
Unblock condition
Any one of: grant remote sessions read access to Randroids-Dojo/VibeKit (add it to the session or its environment so the injected credentials cover the tarball fetch), publish VibeKit to a registry the egress policy already allows, or vendor the pinned tarball. Then prove pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, pnpm typecheck, and the unit suite complete in a fresh remote session, land the deferred Next.js 16.2.11 bump through the normal ledger procedure, and give VibeKit a Detect-new that works without gh from a scope-limited session.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-07-22 by the followup-identity repair slice. Dot VibeBots-f-217-restore-c6ac6142.
Progress update (2026-07-30)
Unblock condition met, by the first of the three listed routes, and it costs one tool call rather than an environment change. The HUD redesign session reproduced the 403 exactly as described on its first pnpm install --frozen-lockfile. Adding randroids-dojo/vibekit to the session's repository scope (the add_repo tool, access: "read") cleared it immediately: the next install exited 0, and pnpm typecheck, pnpm test (1949 passing), pnpm build, pnpm verify (all nine gates), and Playwright all ran in that session. So remote sessions do not need a credential change or a vendored tarball; they need the VibeKit repo added to session scope before the first install, and any agent hitting this can self-serve. Two caveats for whoever closes this: the fix is per session, so it must be repeated each time rather than being a durable environment property, and the Playwright browsers in that container were build 1194 against a config expecting 1223, which is a separate sandbox mismatch worked around with executablePath. Remaining before close: decide whether to make the scope grant part of the environment definition so no session has to rediscover it.

F-215: Persist a bunker claim to its durable row mid-trip, and survive a death

Context
Incremental trip check-ins (2026-07-20) now upload the in-flight trip log (bunker claim included) to the account checkpoint after a claim and every 25 actions, so a reload or another device can resume the pending claim. But the claim is still only durable as a REPLAYABLE LOG against the unchanged world: it does not become a real bunkers row until the surface bank, and a terminal cave-in still resets the trip on resume (replaySavedTrip consumes the collapse), so the claim and dug progress are lost on death. The user's phrasing was "the bunker claim should be sent to the server immediately"; the log check-in satisfies the cross-device and reload half, not the survive-a-death or truly-banked-while-underground half.
Blocker (if any)
Making a claim a durable bunkers row mid-trip means running the anti-cheat validation that only the bank does today (validatePendingBunkerClaim replays the log to the claim move), so it needs a validated mid-trip checkpoint endpoint that replays server-side, plus a mode switch: once a claim is banked mid-trip, its subsequent digs must follow the BANKED path (immediate excavateBunker plus bunker-dig log actions) instead of the pending path, and the two must not double-count at the eventual surface bank. This is the larger "incremental check-in with server replay" arc, not the log-cadence slice.
Unblock condition
Decide whether a mid-trip claim should durably bank into the bunkers row (surviving death) or stay a resumable log. If durable: add a validated checkpoint that replays and persists the claim once, switch that claim to the banked dig path for the rest of the trip, and reconcile so the surface bank neither re-claims nor re-credits. Prove a death after a mid-trip claim keeps the claim and its dug cells while still losing the carried ore (the trip-bag risk model).
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-07-20 by the incremental-trip-check-in slice; the log-cadence half shipped, this durable-claim half is deferred.

F-214: Fold pending bunker digs into the shared trip bag

Context
The trip-bag economy (package 0.1.280) routed BANKED bunker digs into the live shared cargo bag through a logged bunker-dig action, so their ore competes for one capacity and banks at the surface with mine ore. The PENDING (unbanked) claim path was left on its older model: its digs live in the pendingBunker claim payload and settle at bank into a SEPARATE fresh gear-sized bag (settleBunkerDig, capped at one bagful per cash-out), not the live bag. So bunker-ore behavior now differs by whether the claim is banked, which is exactly the branchy inconsistency RULE 7 warns against, and a pending dig does not visibly count up the on-screen bag the way a banked dig does.
Blocker (if any)
None functional; the pending path already requires the walk home, so this is consistency, not a payout hole. Unifying it means the pending claim's digs become bunker-dig log actions too, which changes validatePendingBunkerClaim (today it validates a separately-submitted dug chain) and removes the separate-bag settleBunkerDig call.
Unblock condition
Emit bunker-dig actions for pending-claim digs, derive the pending bunker's dug set from the log rather than a parallel payload field, credit the shared bag inline during replay exactly like the banked path, and retire the fresh-bag settleBunkerDig settle at bank. Keep the one-bunker-per-player and claim-position validation. Prove a pending dig and a banked dig now behave identically (shared bag, surface bank, lost on death) with the same interleaving determinism.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-07-20 by the banked-bunker trip-bag slice (package 0.1.280); the banked half shipped, the pending half is deferred here.
Resolved
Direct commit to main (package 0.1.281, MINE_VERSION 58). A pending-claim dig now credits the SAME shared cargo bag as mine ore through a logged bunker-dig action (excavatePendingBunkerCell in src/state/mine-store.ts now runs the dig through applyAction with the pending-bunker holder and pushes the action), positioned in the log so client and server rebuild the identical bag, and banks only at the surface. At bank the route threads the validated pending bunker as the replay holder (mutually exclusive with the banked path, one bunker per player) and drops the separate-bag settleBunkerDig settle and its bunkerHaulVibes. Anti-cheat: the payload dug set is still adjacency-validated by validatePendingBunkerClaim, and the route now requires its non-pocket dug cells to match the logged bunker-dig cells EXACTLY (both directions), so a forged action cannot credit an undug cell and a claim cannot bank cells whose ore was never carried; the fresh claim's row is inserted with settled_dug = its dug length so nothing re-pays. Chose to keep the payload dug field (adjacency proof) plus the consistency check rather than deriving dug from the log and dropping the field, which stays a possible later simplification. Fixes the F-181 display bug: a bunker-only cash-out no longer reads Sold no resources for N vibes, because the ore is now in trip.soldHaul. New tests: the pending dig logs the action and pays no instant vibes (mine-store), and the bank rejects a pending claim whose logged digs do not match its dug set (route). SIM_VERSION/BUNKER_LAYOUT_VERSION unchanged. The overflow-loot-collection path is still on the vibes shortcut, tracked by F-213.

F-216: Collect bunker overflow loot into the trip bag

Context
When a bunker dig overflows the shared cargo bag, the excess drops as a per-cell loot pile (F-116). Walking over the pile in first person collects it through collectBunkerLoot, which still credits its vibes straight to the balance, the same instant-payout shortcut the trip-bag change (package 0.1.280) removed from digging. So the main dig now rides the bag and pays at the surface, but its own overflow still mints vibes on the spot, which is inconsistent and lets a full bag be drained into vibes underground.

F-212: Prove bunker inventory concurrency against a real database

Context
The atomic bunker write (F-171) is one guarded CTE whose correctness rests on properties only Postgres can execute: the single-statement implicit transaction, the FOR UPDATE row lock that holds the guarded counts still through the debit, and the CTE dependency chain that orders lock before guard before parts write before debit. The server tests mock sql by query string, so they can prove the statement's shape and the app-level contract but cannot run the statement, cannot interleave two clients, and cannot observe rollback. The same limit applies to every other guarded write on this path.
Blocker (if any)
No Postgres in the unit-test environment. Needs a decision on the harness: an ephemeral local Postgres for a separately tagged suite, or a Neon branch used only by a scheduled job. Both add setup that the current fast unit gate deliberately avoids.
Unblock condition
Run the real statement against a real database and prove the interleavings by outcome, not by SQL text: a concurrent purchase plus placement leaves the count raised then debited exactly once; a debit racing a write that lowers the same row never commits a negative count; a stale-revision loser changes neither parts nor inventory; and a failure injected after guard evaluation leaves the row and the bunker revision exactly as they started. Each case reloads authoritative state and asserts revision, parts, and inventory all moved once or all stayed put. Keep the existing shape assertions as the fast gate; this suite is the slow proof behind them.

F-171: Make bunker part and inventory writes atomic

Context
Continuous review of the bunker write path found that saveBunkerAndInventory first commits the revision-guarded bunkers.parts update, then performs six separate absolute-count upserts into player_base_parts. If an inventory statement fails after the bunker write wins, placement can land without its debit or removal can land without its refund. A concurrent purchase can also be overwritten by the stale full inventory snapshot. Resolved F-122 proves that a stale revision loser leaves inventory untouched and receives authoritative state, but it does not cover a winning write that fails partway through persistence.
Blocker (if any)
Resolve before thin bunker slots become player-facing or any part-write path is called transaction-safe. The current whole-cell place and remove routes already use this helper, so the winner-side partial-write risk is live.
Unblock condition
Persist the guarded bunker revision and parts change together with the exact inventory delta in one atomic database operation, such as one statement with a guarded CTE. If the revision loses or any inventory condition fails, neither side may change. Apply deltas against current counts instead of blindly writing a previously loaded absolute snapshot, reject a debit that would go below zero, and return the authoritative bunker and inventory after conflicts. Cover an injected failure after guard evaluation, concurrent purchase plus placement and removal, a stale revision loser, and successful place, remove, and move paths. Each test must reload authoritative state and prove the revision, parts, and inventory either all changed once or all stayed unchanged.
PR / Dot reference
Dot VibeBots-f-171-make-04a3264b under the first-person 3D bunker arc; raised while reviewing PR #230 and the existing F-122 persistence contract.
Resolved
Direct commit to main (no PR). saveBunkerAndInventory now persists the revision-guarded parts write and the inventory change in one atomic statement: a guarded CTE (input deltas, a guard that rejects any debit driving a stored count below zero, the revision-guarded bunkers UPDATE gated on that guard, and a player_base_parts upsert gated on the parts write landing). Inventory moves by delta (count = count + EXCLUDED.count), so a concurrent purchase is added to rather than clobbered by a stale absolute snapshot, and the winner-side partial-write window is closed because Neon runs the single statement in one implicit transaction. The refunding reset keeps its own absolute inventory write (out of scope). Server-only, ships dark. Tests in src/server/bunker.test.ts cover successful place (delta -1), remove (delta +1), and move (zero deltas) issuing exactly one atomic inventory statement in the delta form with the non-negative guard, a losing guard resyncing with no separate write, and an injected mid-write failure leaving no partial second write. The all-or-nothing commit is a property of the single Postgres statement, which the query-string server mock cannot execute.
Debit lock shipped (2026-07-19)
Accepts the post-ship correction raised on PR #279 and closes it. The finding was right: the first shipped guard read player_base_parts.count through an unlocked statement-snapshot LEFT JOIN while the conflict upsert applied its delta to the latest row version, so a write committing in between could commit a count of -1 (the described ordering: a reset pauses before its stale absolute save, a purchase raises the count from zero to one, a place loads that count and passes the guard, the reset writes its earlier zero, and the place then adds -1 to the now-zero row). saveBunkerAndInventory now opens with a locked CTE that selects the affected rows FOR UPDATE in part_id order; guard reads those locked counts instead of a second unlocked read, so the row this statement checks is the row it debits and no concurrent write can move it in between. A part with no row yet cannot be locked, but a debit against a missing row is already rejected by the same guard, so a concurrent insert can only make the check reject conservatively. The dependency chain lock to guard to parts write to debit is unchanged, so a rejected debit still leaves both sides untouched. The reset's separate absolute inventory save remains a lost-update hazard on its own path and stays with F-146, which owns global mutation atomicity; with the lock in place that ordering can now only clobber, never go negative. Tests in src/server/bunker.test.ts add lock coverage (the FOR UPDATE scope, the deterministic ORDER BY p.part_id, the guard reading locked and no longer joining player_base_parts directly, and the lock preceding the guard decision). The correction's request for a real database or faithful concurrency harness is not satisfied by these shape assertions and is carried, unsoftened, by F-212.

F-165: Fail visibly on incompatible bunker wire or stored state

Context
Post-merge review of PR #227 found an unversioned wire break between the already-loaded 0.1.269 client and the 0.1.270 server. The old bundle unconditionally dereferences bunker.core in the first-person grid, core mesh, and flat overlay, while the new server omits that field from both the top-level bunker and activeLiveRaid.bunker. The dismissible version prompt polls only every 60 seconds, and MineSceneErrorBoundary retries the same old bundle, so the player can loop on a blank scene before any refresh guidance appears. The reverse rollback path is unsafe too: the old server expects a stored core object, while new inserts may carry a null core after PR #227 relaxed the database constraint.
Blocker (if any)
Resolve before another bunker wire-shape removal or server rollback. The current deploy-skew window is already live, so failure must be explicit instead of relying on a render exception.
Unblock condition
Add an explicit bunker wire and stored-state compatibility boundary. A request from an unsupported loaded bundle must fail before returning a partial bunker with a stable low-cardinality refresh-required code; the UI must explain that the build is stale and require a full refresh. An incompatible current-version bunker or raid row must fail fast with a clear explanation and a confirmed Start fresh recovery, aligned with F-107, F-117, and Q-022. Cover old-client/new-server and new-client/old-server rollback cases for top-level bunkers and frozen live raids, including how an old server refuses a row whose retired core is null. If a short wire-only bridge is used during rollout, give it an owner and removal condition tied to the confirmed F-117 reset. After that bounded window, remove the every-cold-start ALTER TABLE bunkers ALTER COLUMN core DROP NOT NULL path from normal schema application and reject incompatible rows instead. F-163 remains the separate, explicitly approved physical column deletion. Do not keep permanent silent parsers or runtime migration chains solely for the tiny alpha cohort, and do not include coordinates, raw state, or human text in telemetry.
PR / Dot reference
Dot VibeBots-f-165-fail-1039bd30 under the first-person 3D bunker arc; raised after F-118.
Stored-generation extension (2026-07-15)
Treat an authoritative bunker row that cannot prove the block seed or the authored-pocket layout used to create its dug set as incompatible. Do not silently return no ore for a missing blockSeed, count raw dug.length, or subtract the current pocket from an unversioned older layout. The active F-116 and F-133 successor Dots own the mechanic and achievement acceptance. F-165 owns the stable incompatible-state response and confirmed Start fresh bunker recovery, with no permanent migration chain for the alpha cohort.
Compatibility telemetry extension (2026-07-16)
Make the new in-base recovery observable with one bounded server-derived outcome vocabulary. Record the compatibility operation (load or Start fresh), result (accepted or rejected), and stable reason (current, legacy, unsupported, active raid, stale revision, or storage failure), with the player identifier hashed by the existing monitoring boundary. Do not record seeds, coordinates, parts, dug cells, snapshots, request payloads, or human error text. Route and monitoring tests must keep the response code, telemetry result, and reason aligned, emit no false success for a failed reset, and prove telemetry failure cannot fail or roll back gameplay.
All-operation fail-fast correction (2026-07-16)
Compatibility requires exact equality with the supported layout version. Missing, malformed, older, and newer rows all fail fast, including rollback to an older server. Apply the boundary before every ordinary operation, not only place, move, remove, and excavate. In particular, the existing Reset endpoint must not refund undamaged legacy parts, repair must not spend on a layout that will be wiped, and raid start or settlement must not reward or persist an incompatible snapshot. Only the explicit no-refund Start fresh recovery may cross the boundary; it must forfeit any active raid atomically so an old snapshot cannot settle afterward. Give skin and loot collection an explicit tested policy if they remain available, and return the same stable incompatible code to stale clients on every blocked route.
Authoritative resync correction (2026-07-16)
Treat the stable bunker-incompatible response as an authoritative state transition, not a generic error. A racing structural edit, Reset, repair, raid, bank, or failed Start fresh must either return a current authoritative bunker view that the client adopts or force an explicit reload before any bunker action is re-enabled. A client that believed its bunker was current must expose the Start fresh prompt after the server rejects it as legacy, and a zero-row destructive write must report conflict rather than success. Pin stale-client mutation, future-version rollback, lost-success retry, and reload-failure cases so the client never retains a falsely current marker or continues with stale parts.
Seedless Start fresh recurrence on main (2026-07-16)
Main 9983bffa leaves the stored-generation boundary open. The nullable, unbackfilled block_seed column reads as an undefined blockSeed; applyBunkerStartFresh preserves that value and the guarded SQL never writes block_seed, yet it stamps the row with the current layout_version. That falsely current bunker renders every undug cell as dirt and bunkerCellOreYield returns no reward forever, which can directly explain a live report of old block art with no ore after recovery. Treat a missing or malformed seed as incompatible before first-person entry and every ordinary operation. The confirmed recovery must create an actually fresh generation state in one guarded write: derive and store a valid seed from the authoritative mine world, reset generation-coupled excavation and loot to the authored fresh-state contract, and stamp compatibility together, or fail visibly with guidance to start a fresh state. Do not silently attach a seed to untrusted old dug/loot, and never mark the row current while its seed is absent. Cover a real nullable legacy row through confirmation, compare-and-swap loss, reload, first-person block classification, ore yield, and a bounded missing-block-seed compatibility outcome with no seed or coordinates in telemetry.
User-approved seed-only recovery correction (2026-07-16)
After reviewing the rejected visible-ore proposal and the confirmed seedless row, the user explicitly chose Just fix the seed. This supersedes the preceding fresh-state wipe requirement only when the stored layout is exactly current and the sole generation defect is a missing block_seed. A bounded deterministic repair may preserve existing parts, dug cells, loot, and cosmetics, but it must derive from the authoritative mine world and footprint, compare against the loaded revision, atomically write the seed and advance the revision, and return the authoritative winning row through RETURNING or a reload. A zero-row race, missing or malformed source seed, storage failure, or seedless active-raid snapshot must fail visibly and force authoritative resync instead of returning a locally guessed success. Emit one low-cardinality repair outcome without seeds or cell data, and give the runtime bridge an owner plus removal condition. Every other unsupported wire, layout, or stored-state shape still follows the fail-fast Q-022 boundary.
Reason-vocabulary correction (2026-07-17)
The stable top-level bunker-incompatible response code remains unchanged. Its machine-readable response reason and telemetry reason use exactly current, legacy, unsupported, missing-block-seed, active-raid, stale-revision, or storage-failure. A valid current load is accepted/current; an older or missing layout marker is rejected/legacy; a malformed or future layout or missing or malformed authoritative source is rejected/unsupported; an exactly current row with no valid seed is rejected/missing-block-seed on load; a seedless active raid is rejected/active-raid; a zero-row compare-and-swap loss is rejected/stale-revision; and a database or durable read or write failure is rejected/storage-failure. The narrow seed repair is accepted/missing-block-seed only after the guarded write is proven through RETURNING or authoritative reload. A successful legacy Start fresh recovery may report accepted/legacy only after its separate F-117 transaction is authoritative. Route and monitoring tests must exhaust the complete operation, result, and reason matrix and reject spaces, aliases, unknown tokens, and fallback human text. Keep response reason, telemetry reason, and monitoring aggregate aligned. Keep seeds, coordinates, footprint, cells, parts, dug, loot, snapshots, request payloads, and human text out of telemetry, and prove telemetry failure remains nonfatal to gameplay.

Use the shared tuple (operation_family, logical_request_id, event_kind) as the internal event key. An unexpired identical context replays the stored result and emits no second event; cross-actor reuse, the same token with different inputs, conflicting state, or expired reuse returns a stable rejection and cannot return another actor's result or suppress a legitimate operation under a fresh token. F-147: Cancel held bunker dig repeats on input release

Context
The first-person bunker keeps one strike for a discrete click or tap and automatically restarts while primary input stays held. Releasing an auto-restarted swing before impact clears the held flag but does not cancel that active repeat, so it can dig after release or hit a newly targeted cell. Pointer-lock-unavailable desktop play also lacks blur cleanup for the held action.
Blocker (if any)
Resolve before treating closed F-114 mining input as release-safe on desktop and touch.
Unblock condition
Preserve exactly one initial click or tap strike, even when released before its impact, but mark automatic repeats and cancel an unstruck repeat as soon as its owning input ends. Cover mouseup, pointer-lock loss, unavailable-lock blur, touch pointerup and pointercancel, tool switch, first-person exit, and unmount. Moving the crosshair after release cannot retarget a cancelled repeat. Unit tests pin release around both initial and repeat impacts; browser tests keep open-cell and durable dug counts stable for longer than a full swing and prove no delayed edit request.
PR / Dot reference
Successor to PR #190 source F-135; Dot VibeBots-f-147-cancel-8eefeafc, child of the first-person arc.
Current evidence (2026-07-15)
advanceFpSwing still reports repeat impact before release can cancel it, and the pointer-lock-unavailable blur path still clears movement without owning held-action cleanup.
Port fidelity correction (2026-07-15)
Allocate proof explicitly. Unit cases separately cover release before and after the initial impact, held restart, release before the repeat impact, and no extra strike. Browser cases separately cover desktop mouseup, pointer-lock loss, unavailable-lock blur, touch release and cancel, tool switch, first-person exit, stable open-cell and durable dug counts beyond a full swing, and no delayed edit request.

F-146: Make bunker mutations atomic and serialize every client write

Context
A post-merge review of PR #202 found that its revision guard closes only the first half of F-122. saveBunkerAndInventory commits the guarded bunker update and revision bump before writing inventory in separate statements. Reset likewise writes the bunker before refunds, repair debits the player before writing repaired durability, and other mutations have similar multi-statement ownership. A later failure can therefore leave partial authoritative state whose retry loses the new revision or charges twice. On the client, repair, reset, raid start, raid pickup, and raid finish still bypass serializeEdit, so they can overlap queued structural edits and return responses against different revisions.
Blocker (if any)
Resolve before F-122 can be treated as fully closed and before live raid controls join the first-person bunker.
Unblock condition
Give every bunker mutation one all-or-nothing server write contract across the bunker revision, inventory, player balance, refund, and owned-item rows it changes. Use a single statement, stored operation, or transaction-capable driver path so a failed secondary write commits nothing. Route every client bunker mutation through one explicit write queue or an equivalent mutex, read the freshest revision only when the queued operation starts, and keep local aim and movement responsive. Every stale or conflicting write fails with a stable code plus the complete authoritative view; the client replaces local state and reports the attempted action as failed, without merging two machines. Tests must inject failures after each logical write, overlap a structural edit with repair, reset, and raid controls, reverse delayed responses, retry after resync, and prove exactly one complete result with no duplicate debit, refund, inventory change, or revision bump.

Dot VibeBots-f-146-make-e342a103 (child of VibeBots-first-person-3d-30115c4e).

F-150 owns truthful bunker ore payout totals, visible balance replacement, and balance telemetry. Implement its accepted response and event inside the same all-or-nothing mutation boundary defined here.

The unpublished integration now wires startLiveRaid and resolveLiveRaid into MinePanel before this hard gate is implemented. Start has no pending latch, so rapid taps can issue overlapping unsequenced requests before the external HUD becomes active. The canvas also collects ordinary bunker overflow before computing the raid gate, and a dig swing already in flight can finish after raid start because clearing input flags does not cancel the active swing. An accepted overflow response adopts a new view object for the same raid and currently resets the client sim to tick zero. Also move every collect, dig, place, pry, exit, and start or resolve decision behind one active-raid gate, latch a lifecycle request before its first await, key the runtime by stable raid identity, cancel an in-flight edit animation on accepted start, and prove the server sees no duplicate start or rejected edit churn during combat. Main c84a4403 exposes Start and resolve outside the global client write queue and outside one all-or-nothing server boundary. A remove or reset that reads before Start can refund inventory, then resolve can restore the removed snapshot parts and duplicate stock. A place can consume inventory and be overwritten, and repair can charge vibes before old durability overwrites it. Overflow collection and an in-flight dig can also cross the accepted combat gate. Serialize every bunker mutation and lifecycle request, bind them to one freshest authoritative revision, and pin delayed remove, place, reset, repair, collect, and dig across Start plus resolve with no duplicate or lost inventory, balance, part, or revision.

The draft forfeitLiveRaid client action is another direct mutation outside serializeEdit, with no request latch or raid identity. A delayed second exit request can target a newly started raid, and an equal-revision response can clear newer activeLiveRaid state. Include forfeit or expiry recovery in the one ordered mutation contract, compare the exact active identity at execution and response adoption, and prove delayed exit, new Start, duplicate exit, load, resolve, and edits cannot overwrite one another.

F-176: Make save-slot switches transactional and fail closed

Context
Exact-head review of PR #239 found a general save-slot integrity gap while testing failed rail recovery. switchSaveSlot accepts the remote slot switch and changes activeSlot before the target world and gear are both available. If loadWorld fails without a target local trip, the live mine can still describe the source slot; the unconditional loadGear then begins with persistCurrentTrip() and can save that source state under the target slot key. The function still returns true after failed authority reads, so SaveSlotsPopup navigates to /mine; an offline reload can then resume local state while reporting no authoritative load. This is broader than the elevator-specific F-121 recovery contract.
Blocker (if any)
Resolve before treating save-slot switching or any recovery that changes slots as data-safe. A failed target load must not navigate, overwrite another slot's local trip, or leave the UI claiming a successful switch.
Unblock condition
Stage and validate the target slot's complete world and gear before changing live activeSlot state or persisting under the target key. If either authority read fails, return false, keep the save-slot surface open with visible Retry and Start fresh recovery, and preserve the coherent source slot until a confirmed action. Never call target persistence over source live state. Cover world-read failure, gear-read failure, target local-trip absence, offline reload, no cross-slot localStorage writes, rollback or unchanged source state, and one successful atomic commit. Telemetry must use bounded slot and outcome fields only, never serialized world or gear payloads.
PR / Dot reference
Raised during continuous review of PR #239 exact head 8e10f062. Dot VibeBots-f-176-make-1caf26e2.
PR #242 detached-summary evidence (2026-07-16)
Exact head ac098de9 exposes the same integrity gap outside the explicit switch action. A successful rail reconcile launches loadSaveSlots() without awaiting it, finalizes the pinned marker and global gate, then lets the detached summary response replace activeSlot without loading that slot's world, gear, or rail marker. A delayed slot 2 summary can therefore land after slot 1 recovery and leave active slot 2 over slot 1 authority with the slot 2 marker still stored and the global gate false. Do not let any read-only summary refresh change live activeSlot independently. Either keep summaries informational or stage and atomically commit complete target authority. Add a deferred test that holds the summary request until slot 1 recovery settles, returns slot 2 with its marker set, and proves no mixed-slot state or false unblock. The current PR #242 test returns an invalid empty summary from its catch-all fetch, so it masks this drift. Cross-reference F-121 for the rail recovery gate.

F-192: Guarantee acknowledged elevator outcome delivery

Context

The drain selects unclaimed rows, runs only when a later elevator request arrives, and assumes an unspecified downstream consumer deduplicates raw lines by request id. Rejects remain best-effort. Concurrent drains, a crash between emit and mark, a poison row, or the end of elevator traffic can therefore duplicate, delay indefinitely, starve, or lose the logical outcome even though the accepted row itself exists.
Blocker (if any)

Unblock condition
Persist one bounded accepted or rejected logical outcome per request, claim pending rows atomically with a lease or equivalent concurrency-safe handoff, and retry from an independent scheduled or durable trigger so recovery does not depend on another buy. Implement and verify the real downstream idempotency or acknowledgment boundary instead of assuming deduplication. A crash, slow sink, concurrent drain, partial batch failure, poison row, process restart, or traffic stop must not lose an outcome, duplicate the logical metric, block committed gameplay, or starve later rows. Cover accepted and rejected requests, concurrent drainers, emit-before-mark crash, expired lease, backoff and dead-letter visibility, independent wakeup, bounded identifiers only, and end-to-end sink recovery evidence.

Context

The final diff and required checks did not reject the violation, and the branch merged through ruleset bypass as main 115d8dc6.
Blocker (if any)
Resolve before relying on project ledgers or GDD build logs as a durable audit trail across multi-commit PRs. A final-tree check cannot detect a record that was committed and then silently rewritten inside the same open branch.
Unblock condition
Add a fail-fast validator over every commit from the PR merge base through the exact head. Once committed, a progress article and GDD build-log item must remain byte-for-byte and in order; corrections must be new newest-first records. Existing followup history pairs must remain byte-for-byte while new pairs append, and new primary IDs must stay monotonic. Open-question status, resolution, and movement plus GDD coverage status and reference updates may use only the mutations allowed by their ledger rule; record deletion, identity changes, and reference removal must fail. Report the first offending commit, file, record identity, and exact mutation. Handle base movement and an explicitly approved history replacement without treating a final merge-base diff as proof. Cover a new record, later edit, deletion, reorder, valid correction, permitted status update, reference removal, changed base, and rewritten branch fixture. Run the validator in the required quality gate before review or merge readiness can become green.

Share one module-level crystal geometry or instance the shards so no per-cluster geometry sits under dispose={null}. Warm the actual dirt and rock program variants plus glowing and non-glowing crystal programs before frames start; remove the stale instance-color warm-up path that no longer matches the live meshes. Add desktop and 390x760 mobile browser proof for visible ore, side or vertical face orientation, reveal after opening a neighbor, removal after mining, and no white-card artifact. Repeated entry, exit, reveal, removal, reset, and reload must keep renderer geometry, material, and draw-call counts bounded. Telemetry may retain bounded counts and surface labels, never cell coordinates, ore maps, or raw dug arrays.

No client bunker-haul preview exists even though the pending-dig comment claims pendingBunkerHaulValue supplies one. The identifier has no implementation. F-177: Cancel repeated bunker mining when input is released

Context
The first-person bunker swing preserves one pick strike for a discrete click or tap and auto-restarts while the primary input stays held. After an automatic restart, releasing before that repeat reaches its impact only clears actHeld; the already active repeat still crosses impact, reads the live crosshair, and can dig another cell after release or hit a cell the player retargeted afterward. Pointer-lock-unavailable desktop play also clears movement but not the held action on window blur, so losing the release event can keep repeats armed.
Blocker (if any)
Resolve before treating held first-person mining as release-safe on desktop and touch. A released control must not mutate a second block unexpectedly.
Unblock condition
Keep exactly one strike for the initial discrete click or tap, even when that first press is released before its impact. Mark or otherwise distinguish auto-restarted repeats, then cancel an unstruck repeat as soon as its owning input ends. Cover desktop mouseup, pointer-lock loss, window blur when pointer lock is unavailable, touch pointerup and pointercancel, tool switch, first-person exit, and component unmount. Moving the crosshair after release must not retarget a cancelled repeat. Unit coverage must pin release before and after the initial impact, held restart, release before the repeat impact, and no extra strike. Browser coverage must prove the desktop and touch release paths, pointer-lock loss and unavailable blur, tool switch and exit cleanup, stable open-cell and durable dug counts for longer than one full swing after release, and no delayed edit request.

Dot VibeBots-f-135-cancel-c681ccf0.

F-143: Give turrets a live-raid effect

Context
The first slice of the live raid sim (src/sim/bunker-raid-live.ts, Q-024 option D) implements the dev-described model exactly: Clankers chew blocks, hunt the live player, cross spikes for extra energy, and die when drained. So a turret placed in a bunker currently has zero effect in a live raid, which will read as a broken defense once live raids ship.

Unblock condition
Model turret fire in the live sim: a turret with ammo shoots the nearest in-range Clanker on a fixed cadence (mirror the interim BASIC_TURRET_* constants and tank soak), consuming ammo and either killing or heavily draining the target so it dies and drops its XP pickup. Decide range and line-of-sight in 3D (Chebyshev with axis-aligned sight is the interim shape) and pin it with sim tests: a turret drains ammo, stops Clankers within range, tanks soak the documented shots, and an out-of-ammo turret is inert. Keep it render-only over unchanged colliders; no economy change.
PR / Dot reference
Opened alongside the live raid sim slice; child of the first-person 3D arc.
Resolved
2026-07-15: turret fire modelled in src/sim/bunker-raid-live.ts. Turrets are tracked with ammo; on a fixed cadence (LIVE_TURRET_SHOT_PERIOD_TICKS) each turret with ammo shoots the nearest Clanker within LIVE_TURRET_RANGE along an axis-aligned, unobstructed 3D line of sight (undug rock and standing blocking parts block the shot; spikes and other turrets do not), spending one ammo and adding to the target's soak. A standard or breacher falls to one shot, a tank soaks CLANKER_TANK_TURRET_SHOTS (mirrors the interim resolver), and a stopped Clanker drops its XP pickup. Render-only over unchanged colliders, no economy change. Pinned by four sim tests (shoots and spends ammo, does not fire through rock, inert with no ammo, tank soaks more than a standard). The muzzle/projectile visuals ride with the first-person raid client loop, not here.

F-239: The server never states the post-match teardown

Context
Raised 2026-08-13 by the cleanup review of the tinkerer-depth program. resolveMatch gained a telemetry option and a teardown field (F-225), and runBench uses it, but /api/match/resolve calls resolveMatch(designs, timeLimitTicks) with no options, so the official result always carries teardown: null. The teardown the player reads is therefore entirely client-authored: the arena canvas records its own match and the workshop renders that. The result hash covers the world snapshot plus combat state but not the impact log, so nothing reconciles the two. Under the Q-003 hybrid-authority contract, post-match damage attribution is currently the one match fact the server never states.
Blocker (if any)
None technical. It is a cost and product decision, not a cleanup: recording telemetry on every official match adds per-match server work, and the honest alternatives (serve the server's teardown, or stop offering the field on the route) differ in what the player is shown after a verified fight.
Unblock condition
Ready once that call is made. Either pass { telemetry: true } from the route and have the workshop prefer the server's teardown when verification succeeds, or drop the field from the route response so the API stops implying it. Acceptance: whichever is chosen, a verified match shows a teardown whose provenance is unambiguous, and the choice is recorded here.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-08-13 during the tinkerer-depth cleanup pass.
Resolved
2026-08-13: took the first option. /api/match/resolve now reruns with { telemetry: true } and returns the teardown, so post-match damage attribution is a fact the authority states rather than something only the client computed. Recording is bounded (the log caps at 4096 impacts and reuses slots) and trivial next to the 3600 physics steps the rerun already pays for. The workshop adopts the server's teardown ONLY when the hashes agree: on a mismatch the two sheets describe different fights, so showing the official one would hide the disagreement rather than surface it, and the local sheet stays. The sheet labels its own provenance ("official" or "local run") so the player can see which they are reading. Covered by a route test asserting the response carries a teardown with both bots, their parts in design order, and a non-zero impact count.

F-238: Decide whether gear ratios are a range or a fixed set

Context
Raised 2026-08-13 by the cleanup review. connectionSchema validates gearRatio against a continuous range (MIN_GEAR_RATIO 0.5 to MAX_GEAR_RATIO 2.5), while the workshop only ever offers the four presets in GEAR_RATIO_PRESETS (0.7, 1, 1.6, 2.2). So the buildable set and the acceptable set are different rules, and the server is the looser one: a design authored by hand and posted to /api/match/resolve with gearRatio: 2.5 validates and fights with more reduction than any bot a player can construct in the workshop. The presets were moved into src/sim/design.ts in the cleanup so both rules are at least visible in one file, but they still disagree.
Blocker (if any)
None, and it is deliberately not fixed in the cleanup pass because tightening the schema to preset membership is a behaviour change, not a simplification. Nothing has shipped with gearing yet, so there is no migration cost to deciding either way now.
Unblock condition
Ready: decide whether arbitrary ratios in range are intended (a future workshop slider, or player-authored designs being welcome) or whether the presets are the rule. If the presets are the rule, validate membership in GEAR_RATIO_PRESETS instead of the range, matching how weight classes are enforced server-side rather than trusted from the client. Acceptance: a design carrying an off-preset ratio is either accepted deliberately or rejected with a named issue, and a test pins the choice.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-08-13 during the tinkerer-depth cleanup pass.
Resolved
2026-08-13: the presets are the rule. MIN_GEAR_RATIO and MAX_GEAR_RATIO are gone and connectionSchema validates membership in GEAR_RATIO_PRESETS through isGearRatioPreset, so the server accepts exactly what the workshop can build and a hand-authored design can no longer fight with reduction no player has access to. This matches how weight classes are enforced, for the same reason: the client is not trusted to keep to its own options. The rule has one home; validateDesign still owns the separate question of which connections may carry a ratio at all. Covered by a schema test over every preset plus five off-preset values, and a route test proving a posted design with an unavailable ratio is rejected with a 400.

Tightening the ceiling from 2.5 to the top preset 2.2 silently broke a property the power cost existed to create, which is worth recording because a test caught it rather than review: GEAR_POWER_PER_RATIO 12 was calibrated so two axles at maximum reduction cost more than a weapon-carrying bot's spare power (the saw bot has 30 to spare, and 2 x 1.5 x 12 = 36 priced it out). At the 2.2 ceiling that becomes 2 x 1.2 x 12 = 28.8, which fits inside 30, so maximum torque and a big weapon became affordable together and the whole point of the cost lapsed. Re-derived to 13 (2 x 1.2 x 13 = 31.2) to restore the original intent under the new ceiling, with the constant's comment now naming the dependency so the two are re-derived together. The saw bot is priced out of the top preset and still affords the middle one, which is the intended budget rather than a ban.

F-237: The drivetrain is torque limited, so reduction gearing is close to a free win

Context
Measured 2026-08-12 by the new bench (F-226) while landing gearing (F-229), and worth recording because it was found by instrument rather than by argument. Benching the starter Rammer across the six stock bots at four ratios: 0.6 gives a 33% win rate and 74.67 average damage dealt, stock (ratio 1) gives 17% and 91.95, 1.5 gives 33% and 106.98, and 2.5 gives 67% and 133.2. Damage dealt rises almost monotonically with reduction. The cause is that setDriveVelocity's default motor factor of 50 cannot hold the commanded 12 rad/s against the bots' mass and friction, so the drivetrain is torque limited and the commanded top speed almost never binds. Raising the motor factor (which reduction does) therefore buys speed AND shove, and the intended speed-for-torque trade does not appear in a straight-line run: measured distances over 300 ticks were 1.06 at ratio 0.5, 1.64 stock, 6.72 at 1.5, and 7.57 at 2.5.
Blocker (if any)
None, and gearing shipped without waiting on this: the power cost added in the same slice (GEAR_POWER_PER_RATIO) makes torque compete with the weapon for the core budget, so it is a real trade at build time even while it stays strong at run time. The saw bot, for example, cannot afford maximum reduction. What is NOT yet true is that a tall gear costs you anything in the fight itself.
Unblock condition
Ready: raise the base motor authority so a stock bot actually reaches its commanded speed, which makes the top-speed cap bind and turns reduction into a genuine trade, then re-bench every stock design and the replica roster to re-tune. This changes the physics of every existing fight, so it bumps SIM_VERSION and regenerates the golden vectors, and it should land beside the degradation work (F-232) rather than alone, since both retune the same feel. Acceptance: at equal power a speed-geared build wins a straight-line race and loses a shoving contest against a torque-geared one, both proven by unit tests, and the bench shows no single ratio dominating the stock roster.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-08-12 during the build-and-battle depth program, by the bench built two slices earlier.
Resolved
2026-08-14: there is no imbalance to fix. The dominance this entry exists to describe was an artifact of the measuring instrument, not a property of the game.

The bench ran each design against six opponents from ONE fixed starting position, and the sim is fully deterministic, so a matchup had exactly one outcome forever. A "win rate" was therefore six fixed results with no variance behind it and 16.7-point granularity, and the differences being chased were one or two matches. Fixed by giving matches a starting arrangement (SPAWN_ARRANGEMENTS in combat.ts, selected by MatchOptions.variation, with index 0 reproducing the historical spawn byte for byte) and teaching the bench to fight every opponent from several of them.

Re-measured with 36 matches per preset instead of 6: ratio 0.7 wins 44%, ratio 1 wins 50%, ratio 1.6 wins 61%, and ratio 2.2 wins 58%. The spread is 17 points rather than 50, and the top preset is not even the strongest. Gearing is already balanced, with a mild tilt toward reduction that the power cost is there to price. The one real signal is that reduction produces markedly more decisive fights (8 wins by disable against 1 to 3 for the others), which is a good property, not a problem.

Nothing about the sim changed: SIM_VERSION stays 6, no golden vector moved, and an unvaried match is identical to every match previously recorded. The workshop bench now fights three arrangements per opponent by default, so the number a player reads has samples behind it.
Levers tested and rejected
Recorded so none of these is re-attempted. Raising base motor authority (the original prescription): no effect on the top preset, 83% before and after on the old instrument. Raising the timeout scoring weight for pressure from 25 to 150: literally zero change, because pressureTicks requires closing velocity while in range and in a tight arena both bots are in contact rather than closing, so the stat barely accrues and scaling nothing by six is still nothing. Widening the arena from 9 to 15 with proportional spawns: this DID move the old number (83% to 50%), which is what first suggested the mechanism, but it works by reducing contact and so undoes the tight-brawl decision from F-063. Decoupling steering authority from the gear ratio: rejected on measurement, because the yaw advantage reduction enjoys is not a bug. It comes from grip (measured slip is 0.16 at ratio 0.7 against 0.01 at ratio 2.2), it holds at every motor factor from 25 to 800, and a slower-geared drivetrain genuinely having more traction margin is correct physics that should not be broken to chase a symptom.
Diagnosis corrected 2026-08-14
The premise of this entry is WRONG and the prescribed fix must not be applied. It was inferred from straight-line distance runs that were confounded two ways: the arena wall sits 9 units out and bots spawn at the centre, so every run longer than about 8.2 units was measuring the wall rather than the drivetrain, and the starter bot is transiently unstable off the line, which made short runs read as chaotic rather than slow. Re-measured directly.

The drivetrain is NOT torque limited. Driving straight at the current motor factor of 50, the wheels settle at 11.0 rad/s against a commanded 12, which is 92%, with 5% slip. Raising the motor factor from 50 to 1000 moves that to 12.1 rad/s, a gain of about 4%. Motor authority is not the constraint on top speed and never was.

Gearing already trades speed exactly as designed. Measured steady-state linear speed at the current factor: ratio 0.7 gives 3.99, ratio 1 gives 3.54, ratio 1.6 gives 2.55, and ratio 2.2 gives 1.88. That is monotonic, and reduction costs roughly 45% of top speed. The straight-line race half of the acceptance condition below is therefore ALREADY MET, and has been all along: over a fixed window a speed-geared build covers 7.1 units against a torque-geared build's 3.9.

Applying the prescribed fix would make things worse, not better. Benched across the full stock roster at the four buildable presets, raising the motor factor from 50 to 300 leaves the dominance completely untouched: ratio 2.2 wins 83% of matches either way. All it does is lift the ungeared build from 33% to 50%, flattening the three lower presets against each other while the top preset still dominates. It would change every physics result in the game, force a SIM_VERSION bump and a golden regeneration, and not address the problem it was written to address.
What the imbalance actually is
Reduction does not win by out-running or out-shoving. It wins by taking less damage: at the current factor the top preset averages 96.85 damage taken against the ungeared build's 111.62, while dealing 159.99 against 108.61. The extra motor authority buys stability and control, and a small close-quarters arena rewards control while giving top speed almost nothing to do. Head-to-head shove and push rigs were built to quantify this and are NOT trustworthy: midpoint drift is polluted by both bots skating together, and driving into a station-holding defender measures the arrival impulse rather than sustained push, which produced non-monotonic nonsense (a 5.2 unit "push" from the FASTER attacker at one factor). The bench, which runs complete deterministic matches, is the only instrument here that gave repeatable answers, and it is what the numbers above come from.
Superseded unblock condition
The condition below (raise base motor authority, re-tune, bump SIM_VERSION) is retained as history and must not be actioned. The live question is a balance decision, not a physics fix, and it needs a product call: either price reduction harder than the current GEAR_POWER_PER_RATIO does, or give it a cost that bites in a fight rather than only at build time (slower turning is the obvious candidate, since the controller scales steer through the same motor), or accept that a control build beating a fast build is correct for combat robots and the remaining issue is only that it is strictly better rather than differently good. Whichever is chosen, the bench across all four presets is the acceptance instrument, and "no single preset dominates the stock roster" stays the target.
Measurement refresh 2026-08-13
The figures above predate both damage degradation (F-232) and the preset cap (F-238), so they are kept as the original evidence and superseded here. Re-benched against the current sim across the four buildable presets: 0.7 gives a 50% win rate and 97.69 average damage, 1 gives 33% and 108.61, 1.6 gives 50% and 95.59, and 2.2 gives 83% and 159.99. The top preset is still the strongest by a wide margin, so this followup stands unchanged; what has changed is that reduction now costs power at build time, which bounds the problem without fixing it.

F-232: Damage degradation short of destruction

Context
Raised 2026-08-12 by the tinkerer-audience design pass. Parts are binary: full strength until zero health, then gone. That erases the most legible failure mode a mechanic knows, the part that still works but works worse. The combat GDD already lists this under what this does NOT cover yet (weakened motors, armour, damage types).
Blocker (if any)
None. It is a SIM_VERSION bump and it interacts with every stock matchup, so it should land after the bench (F-226) exists to measure the balance change rather than guess at it.
Unblock condition
Ready: derive a per-part effectiveness from its health ratio, apply it to drive motor velocity and spinner motor velocity, and surface the degraded state in the teardown and the HUD. Acceptance: a wheel at low health measurably slows its side in a unit test, the effect is monotonic in health, golden vectors are regenerated in the same slice with a recorded reason, and the bench shows the balance delta across the stock roster.
PR / Dot reference
Raised 2026-08-12 during the build-and-battle depth program.
Resolved
2026-08-12: shipped. partEffectiveness falls linearly from 1 at full health to MIN_PART_EFFECTIVENESS 0.35 at zero (not to zero: a part on its last hit point should still work, badly, or the final sliver of health would be worthless). Drive velocity is scaled by the mean effectiveness of the mobility parts still attached, and spinner axles are driven every tick at the blade effectiveness through the new setSpinVelocity, so a chewed-up saw winds down instead of staying lethal until the frame it breaks. Disabled bots now stop their spinners as well as their drive. This genuinely changes physics, so SIM_VERSION goes 5 to 6 and the goldens were regenerated with a recorded reason. The regeneration surfaced a coverage gap the gate is designed to catch: the only combat vector was Rammer versus Brawler, which has no spinner and never damages a wheel, so it could not observe the change at all; GOLDEN-COMBAT-0002 (saw versus drums) was added to lock the new behaviour in. Bench measurement across the stock roster: the starter Rammer moved from a 17% win rate, 91.95 average damage and zero decisive wins to 33%, 108.61 and its first win by disable. Verified by 7 unit tests plus the regenerated goldens. A real crash was found by running the bench and is fixed here with its own regression test: processDeaths removed a destroyed part joint from axleJoints but never from spinJoints, which was harmless while spinners were configured once at assembly and became a use-after-free the moment they were driven every tick, crashing the WASM side when the world was freed.

Blocker (if any)

Bumps SIM_VERSION. Acceptance: an over-massed weapon on a weak mount detaches in a unit test while the same weapon on a strong mount holds, and no torn part gains velocity beyond the existing destruction case.
